video_title: Giannis Rumors HEAT Up, Jalen Duren's Contract Conundrum, Crazy Draft Change

quotes.speaker: Keith Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren's All-NBA nod makes him eligible for a 30% max contract
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Duren is now eligible for a 30% of the cap max, which would start at 49.5 million.
quotes.quote: Jalen Duren is now eligible for a 30% of the cap max, which would start at 49.5 million and essentially go up from there and that would give him 287 million dollars over five years. Previous max, if he had not made All-NBA, would have been 239 over five years. So we're talking a difference of 48 million that would be the difference there. His max with another team, because remember, he is a restricted free agent. So if the Bulls or the Lakers or the Nets, because those are our three cap space teams right now, wanted to parachute in with a full max offer sheet for Jalen Duren, for 177. So that's 110 million dollars less and also one year less, because you can only get four years with another team.

quotes.speaker: Keith Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Keith Smith questions if the Pistons should offer Jalen Duren a full max contract
quotes.excerpt: I don't think he's going to touch the 287 number. I think that's just insanely high.
quotes.quote: I don't think he's going to touch the 287 number. I think that's just insanely high. That's really a lot of money for Jalen Duren, all things considered. I think the Pistons are going to kind of say, well, wait, what are we doing here? This seems like it's too much money. That's an average of 57 million dollars over five years. That's just too much. It just doesn't fit all just starts to fall apart. I think what they're going to do is say, I threw out the number I think that is fair for Jalen Duren is five, 185. That'd be 37 million a year. It's not even the full 25% of the cap max. And what I would be pitching to Jalen Duren is, hey, we don't want to be one of these other teams that has two, three, four guys locked in and we're having to shed talent because we can't put the right guys around you and Cade Cunningham.

quotes.speaker: Keith Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Keith Smith believes Austin Reaves will get a larger contract than Jalen Duren
quotes.excerpt: I think it's going to be Austin Reaves, because I think there is a chance the Lakers are just going to max him.
quotes.quote: I think it's going to be Austin Reaves, because I think there is a chance the Lakers are just going to max him. I feel a little more confident that he is going to be at least a really, really good regular season player, who can be the focal point of my offense in the regular season and get me through those games. And Duren, we saw moments of that, but he's not, he's not Jokic, he's not Wemby, he's not that kind of, just throw it to him, even though he's a center, he can make things happen kind of guy. And the other key is, Duren is not like a threatening to make all defensive teams. He's much improved on the defensive end, but I just worry when my center is not a great defensive player as well.

quotes.speaker: Keith Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo's contract situation gives him significant leverage to steer his next destination
quotes.excerpt: Giannis is going to have a lot of ability to steer his destination because he has the threat of free agency looming in 2027.
quotes.quote: Giannis is going to have a lot of ability to steer his destination because he has the threat of free agency looming in 2027. The Miami thing's been looming for close to five years now. That was out there before he signed his current contract. Miami is, I always say, they're Lakers East. If there's a good player available, the Heat are going to be interested in it. And I don't even say that, that isn't, I'm not being snarky or snide when I say that, that's just kind of how it works. They're two very desirable destinations that players like to be and they are consistently doing what they can to be involved and trying to get those players. The Boston stuff, there's two parts that if you've been paying a lot of attention, that are very interesting here. Giannis, near the end of the regular season, kind of out of nowhere, just heaped all this praise on Joe Mazzulla as a coach. Brad Stevens at his end of season media availability, harped on multiple times, yeah, we have been a team that shoots a lot of three-pointers. We'd like to have a lot more dunks and layups, but we don't have the guys. We have not given Joe Mazzulla a roster that has guys who get dunks and layups. And that's what we want to be. We want to be a team that can be more versatile, play more inside. And instantly everybody went to, well, there's a guy who gets a lot of dunks and layups available. How do we get there? And then you've got the Jaylen Brown stuff. If you want to get Giannis, it's either put together a big package of stuff going out or you have the one big salary, and in Boston's case, Jaylen Brown. It's like a million dollars difference in their salaries. And Boston, because they're under, they're now under the tax, but it's really because they're under the first apron, they could plus that up with just any one minimum guy and that makes it work. There's been even more reporting that Giannis probably isn't ever going to come out and say I want a trade because it doesn't need to be said at this point. Now it is just, it's basically going to be, you're going to extend, you're not, and that you don't need to ask for a trade. We're just going to move on with a trade. Four weeks from today is the first round of the NBA Draft. And the Bucks have said they want to have it done by draft day. I continue to believe Giannis is going to get traded. My bet would be one of the teams that's been mentioned. There was a thought out there of, hey, everybody's now like, we got to combat Wemby if you want to win, whether that's win the title or just get through the West. And a lot of teams are like, well, there's one guy in the league that can kind of power through Wemby that exists and that's Giannis. So why not go get him?

quotes.speaker: Keith Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell's contract dilemma for Cavaliers: risk or trade
quotes.excerpt: It makes complete sense why Donovan Mitchell would want to wait. If you're Mitchell, this is probably my last max contract. Yeah, I want the full max.
quotes.quote: It makes complete sense why Donovan Mitchell would want to wait. If you were, let's say Donovan Mitchell had been with you all 10 years and you were still and you're competing for titles and everything was great and all is good, then you probably, you put your faith in that trust of, all right, we've been down this road for 10 years together, we're just going to, we we get it, we're going to let it roll and then we'll get it done next summer. I think the challenge is, Mitchell can say he loves it there, but how do you prove you love it there? Well, you sign today then. And what I would be doing if I'm the Cavs, I'd be like, hey, no, the team that just beat us, and the guy who just whipped our tails, Jalen Brunson, he didn't tell the Knicks I need every single penny you can give me. He said, I will take a lot of money, but I'm going to leave some on the table so we can have Bridges and we can have Harden and we can have Anunoby and we can have Towns. We can have all these guys. That's going to be a conversation this summer where it is, hey, we all left money on the table, keep Mitchell Robinson, right? We, yeah, you're going to have to pay the tax, probably going to be a second apron team, but we don't need a whole lot else. We've got everything we need here in the building, let's just go. So I think what we're going to see here with the Cavs is, I think you have to at least say, hey, do you need an extra 8.7 million in year one? And then that'll total up to tens of millions of dollars over the course of a five-year deal. Or can we do it just now and you start a little bit lower and we go. You're still going to get the max because he's Donovan Mitchell, he's awesome. We're still going to max you, but do you need it? And if you're Mitchell, this is probably my last max contract. Yeah, I want the full, the full max. So it's, it is tough. This is why NBA GMs make an awful lot of money is because these are the difficult decisions you have to make because it makes complete sense why Donovan Mitchell would want to wait. I'm not by any means saying if Donovan Mitchell says, now I want to wait, then you have to immediately turn around and trade him, because he is at least giving you the, this is where I want to be. But I would have to feel really good by the trade deadline of, he's not just going to turn and walk on us this summer if I'm not going to trade him then. If you roll the dice on that and the season doesn't go well, that's a bad, bad spot. One of the most damaging things that can happen to an NBA team, aside from like catastrophic injury of course, is a superstar player walks away with no return coming back. It takes years to recover from something like that. And that's why teams, they can't, they cannot have it. They can't allow players to have that kind of power over their franchise. It's why Giannis is probably going to wind up getting traded. It's an interesting, I think this is one of the more interesting subplots of the summer, what happens here with the Cavs and Donovan Mitchell. The good thing is, Donovan Mitchell is saying he wants to stay. Although, you know what, I'm contradicting myself here because on the flip side, if Donovan Mitchell was giving no indication he wanted to stay, and if he wouldn't sign an extension, then we the Cavs have certainty. They know what they're doing. They're trading Donovan Mitchell and that's that. The Cavs either have to, if Mitchell says I need the 35% max, and I will sign it with you next summer, but you have to trust me, then the Cavs have to either roll the dice or trade him. And that that could be a difficult decision either way.

quotes.speaker: Keith Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Keith Smith explains the proposed NBA Draft credit system
quotes.excerpt: Each team is going to get 100 draft credits each draft. Easiest way to think of this is if you've ever done an auction draft in a fantasy league.
quotes.quote: This was reported by The Athletic, Mike Vorkunov, who's been all over all things like business of the NBA for years now. He does a really good job with stuff like that. So we all know they're calling what they're calling the 3-2-1 system, right? That's what they're voting on, where it is, there's these tiers of teams where they have three lottery balls, two or one lottery ball, and that's how it goes. That is being tweaked and voted on. They expect that to be voted on, that will take effect next draft, not this one, not 2026, but for 2027 and beyond. But the league is saying, they're basically going to take each team is going to get 100 draft credits each draft. Easiest way to think of this is if you've ever done an auction draft in a fantasy league, you basically have those credits and you can start bidding for picks. So if you are like, it's Wemby's draft, you're going to have all 30 teams are going to be like, 100 credits in, everything I got. And then what happens is, then it sounds like, because there's other stuff that is built off this, if there are, in that case, all 30 teams, then there will be some kind of lottery system to decide who gets them. If a team's like, you know what, I'm not going to be one out of 30 chances, I'm going to hold back and I'm going to only put in 10. Well, you're not going to be a part of it, but then you'll still have credits to use later when you bid for other picks. So that is what the kind of kind of offer is there. The other thing is teams would trade those credits. So instead of trading picks, you would trade, we're going to give you 40 of our credits. And that's what you would put in there. You would put those in, those credits to try to try to get forward. So you could pile up credits moving forward, which actually, I wrote about an idea like this, I called them chances, I didn't call them credits, for Yahoo years ago, probably. Six years ago probably. You're not, it's because in this world where a pick is gone, a pick is gone. There's almost no real way to get your picks back. Like now it becomes, all right, well, we could still kind of re, you know, kind of rejigger the odds a little bit by trading some stuff out and getting it back. So I think it would be interesting. It'd be kind of fun. I mean, one more thing we would all be able to track and like, who, how many credits do they have? Where did they get those credits from? I guess requests like they have to be traded in batches of five or 10. Because I don't want to be tracking like, they have 194 credits and this team has 412. Definitely no decimals. That's too much. And we would have to come up with something cool to name it. Because just credits don't sound. We need to come up with something else. We need to come up with something else. I don't know. Like maybe it's a way to to give a, a shout out to a like an NBA legend or or something like that. Like, I don't know. Trade, are you going to trade 75 Dr. J bucks or something? Kobe bucks or something or or whatever, you know. Yeah, who's like, yeah, like we, I don't know, we work some guy who was supposed to be awesome in the draft, but wasn't. Like, you know, like that's how you get it like, like just to just to honor that guy still. Anthony Bennett bucks. Yeah, yeah, Bennett bucks. Yeah, Bennett dollars. Nobody wants those. Your Olo Wakanda dollars. Oh no. Oh man. You know what though, Keith, we're accidentally stumbling our way into Schrubucks here. Yeah, that's it. That's it. What's the value of one Schrubuck? What's the ratio of one Schrubuck to one Stanley dollar? It's the same as the ratio of unicorns to leprechauns. Stanley Nickels. Stanley Nickels. That's right. Stanley Nickels. Yeah.
